title: Rigveda 3.15: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 3.15: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 3.15 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 3, the family book of Viśvāmitra. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 199r-200r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 3.15.1-4 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 1, varga 15); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 199v
translation.original_text:
1vi pāja̍sā pṛ̱thunā̱ śośu̍cāno̱ bādha̍sva dvi̱ṣo ra̱kṣaso̱ amī̍vāḥ | su̱śarma̍ṇo bṛha̱taḥ śarma̍ṇi syām a̱gner a̱haṁ su̱hava̍sya̱ praṇī̍tau ||
2tvaṁ no̍ a̱syā u̱ṣaso̱ vyu̍ṣṭau̱ tvaṁ sūra̱ udi̍te bodhi go̱pāḥ | janme̍va̱ nitya̱ṁ tana̍yaṁ juṣasva̱ stoma̍m me agne ta̱nvā̍ sujāta ||
3tvaṁ nṛ̱cakṣā̍ vṛṣa̱bhānu̍ pū̱rvīḥ kṛ̱ṣṇāsv a̍gne aru̱ṣo vi bhā̍hi | vaso̱ neṣi̍ ca̱ parṣi̱ cāty aṁha̍ḥ kṛ̱dhī no̍ rā̱ya u̱śijo̍ yaviṣṭha ||
4aṣā̍ḻho agne vṛṣa̱bho di̍dīhi̱ puro̱ viśvā̱ḥ saubha̍gā saṁjigī̱vān | ya̱jñasya̍ ne̱tā pra̍tha̱masya̍ pā̱yor jāta̍vedo bṛha̱taḥ su̍praṇīte ||
translation.text:
1RESPLENDENT with thy wide-extending lustre, dispel the terrors of the fiends who hate us May lofty Agni be my guide and shelter, the easily-invoked, the good Protector.
2Be thou To us, while now the morn is breaking, be thou a guardian when the Sun hath mounted.. Accept, as men accept a true-born infant, my laud, O Agni nobly born in body.
3Bull, who beholdest men, through many mornings, among the dark ones shine forth red, O Agni. Lead us, good Lord, and bear us over trouble: Help us who long, Most Youthful God, to riches.
4Shine forth, a Bull invincible, O Agni, winning by conquest all the forts and treasures, Thou Jâtavedas who art skilled in guiding, the chief high saving sacrifice's Leader.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 199v (numbered 9v by the scribe) (OPenn image 201, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 3.15.1 ‹-śarmaṇi syām agneḥ aham›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 200r (numbered 10r by the scribe), begins in RV 3.15.5 ‹rathaḥ na sasniḥ abhi›. Verses 3.15.1-4 end on this page; 3.15.1 begins on fol. 199r (numbered 9r by the scribe).

translation.original_ref: RV 3.15.5-7 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 1, varga 15); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 200r
translation.original_text:
5acchi̍drā̱ śarma̍ jaritaḥ pu̱rūṇi̍ de̱vām̐ acchā̱ dīdyā̍naḥ sume̱dhāḥ | ratho̱ na sasni̍r a̱bhi va̍kṣi̱ vāja̱m agne̱ tvaṁ roda̍sī naḥ su̱meke̍ ||
6pra pī̍paya vṛṣabha̱ jinva̱ vājā̱n agne̱ tvaṁ roda̍sī naḥ su̱doghe̍ | de̱vebhi̍r deva su̱rucā̍ rucā̱no mā no̱ marta̍sya durma̱tiḥ pari̍ ṣṭhāt ||
7iḻā̍m agne puru̱daṁsa̍ṁ sa̱niṁ goḥ śa̍śvatta̱maṁ hava̍mānāya sādha | syān na̍ḥ sū̱nus tana̍yo vi̱jāvāgne̱ sā te̍ suma̱tir bhū̍tv a̱sme ||
translation.text:
5Lighting Gods hither, Agni, wisest Singer, bring thou to us many and flawless shelters. Bring vigour, like a car that gathers booty: bring us, O Agni, beauteous.Rarth and Heaven.
6Swell, O thou Bull and give those powers an impulse, e'en Earth and Heaven who yield their milk in plenty, Shining, O God, with Gods in clear effulgence. Let not a mortal's evil will obstruct us.
7Agni, as holy food to thine invoker, give wealth in cattle, lasting, rich in marvels. To us be born a son and spreading offspring. Agni, be this thy gracious will to us-ward.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 200r (numbered 10r by the scribe) (OPenn image 201, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 3.15.5 ‹rathaḥ na sasniḥ abhi›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 200v (numbered 10v by the scribe), begins in RV 3.16.3 ‹tuvi-dyumna varṣiṣṭhasya prajāvataḥ anamīvasya›. Verses 3.15.5-7 end on this page; 3.15.5 begins on fol. 199v (numbered 9v by the scribe).
